messages.content: Why does it matter how I apply fertiliser so it is not wasted?

Band or place fertiliser near the plant rather than broadcasting it. Broadcast urea on a hot dry surface loses a large share to the air before the plant sees it. Testing before buying fertiliser is cheaper than guessing. Blanket application wastes money on nutrients the soil already has and misses the one that is actually limiting.

How do I raise tilapia in a pond?

Tilapia breed readily in ponds, which crowds the pond with small fish. Mono-sex stocking or managing recruitment is what keeps them growing to size. Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, but only if Newcastle vaccination is kept up. Unvaccinated flocks are periodically wiped out. Raised slatted floors keep goats off wet bedding and reduce foot rot and worm burden. Compare a treated strip against an untreated one, otherwise you cannot tell whether the weather did it.
What grows well in sudan conditions?

Single season, roughly 500 to 1000mm. Sorghum, millet, cowpea, groundnut, some maize with fertiliser. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake.

My groundnuts got rained on while drying. They look fine now that they are dry. Can I still sell them?

Be careful here, because looking fine is not the same as being safe.

Groundnut that dries slowly, or gets wetted again part way through drying, is the classic route to aflatoxin. It is a mould toxin, it is not visible at levels that still matter, and it does not go away once the nuts dry out. It causes real harm to people and animals, and it is the usual reason a consignment gets rejected at a formal buyer.

What I would do:

1. Sort hard. Discard every nut that is shrivelled, discoloured, mouldy or damaged. That sorting removes a large share of the risk.
2. Get them fully dry now and keep them dry, in ventilated storage off the ground.
3. If you are selling to a buyer who tests, ask about testing before you commit a large quantity.

For future harvests the defence is speed. Lift, dry fast on a tarpaulin or raised platform rather than bare ground, and get them under cover before rain. Once the toxin is there, there is nothing you can add to remove it.
What is the right way to decide about dry season production?

Dry season vegetable production under irrigation usually earns more than wet season production, because supply is short and prices are higher. Band or place fertiliser near the plant rather than broadcasting it. Broadcast urea on a hot dry surface loses a large share to the air before the plant sees it. Alternate legumes and cereals. It breaks pest and disease cycles and cuts nitrogen cost.
My cassava is underperforming. Where do I start?

Weed control in the first 3 months determines yield more than any other single factor, because cassava canopies late and cannot compete early. 1m by 1m for sole crop, about 10,000 plants per hectare. Wider at 1m by 1.5m when intercropping with maize. Improved varieties such as TME 419, TMS 30572 and TMS 98/0505 offer mosaic resistance and higher root yield than most local landraces. Stem cuttings 20 to 25cm long with at least 5 nodes, taken from the middle of mature stems 8 to 12 months old. Never cut from a plant showing mosaic symptoms.
Sorry, what does that mean exactly?

Ridges or mounds on heavy or waterlogged soil to prevent root rot. Flat planting is acceptable on free-draining sandy loam. 9 to 12 months for early varieties, up to 18 months for late. Roots left too long become woody and lose starch quality. The short version is to treat what is causing it rather than what you can see.

My cassava leaf dey yellow and e twist. I don spray insecticide but nothing change.

Make you stop to spend money for spray. Na cassava mosaic disease be dat, and no insecticide fit cure am.

Na virus. Whitefly dey carry am, but the main way e dey enter na through the stem wey you plant. If you cut your stem from plant wey get the sickness, the farm don carry am before e even germinate. Na why the spray no do anything.

Wetin you go do:

1. This season own don happen. Comot the plant wey bad well well.
2. This one important: no ever cut planting stem from plant wey dey show this sign. Cut from healthy strong plant, from the middle of stem wey don reach eight to twelve months.
3. Try get improved variety like TME 419 or TMS 30572 wey fit resist am.

Clean planting material na the whole control.

How do I stop stem borers coming back next season?
1. Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone.
I have fall armyworm but my maize is already tasselling. Should I spray?

Probably not. Fall armyworm costs you yield mainly in early vegetative growth, when the plant is small and the whorl is the growing point. On a tasselled crop the damage it can still do rarely repays the price of the spray.

What is worth doing at this stage:

1. Leave it and protect your cash.
2. Plan the residue clean-up now. Destroy the stalks after harvest instead of leaving them standing, because that is what carries the pest into next season.
3. Scout early next season, in the first weeks, rather than waiting for visible damage.

If the infestation is severe and the crop is still filling, ask your extension officer to look at it before you decide.
What is the right way to dry produce faster and cleaner?

A simple raised solar dryer dries faster and cleaner than open ground and keeps rain, dust and animals off the crop. Faster drying is directly less mould. Packaging is not decoration. Grading and clean uniform packs get a better price for the same produce and reduce rejection. Hermetic bags control storage insects without chemicals, but only if the liner is sealed properly every time.
I want to apply fertiliser so it is not wasted. What should I know?

Band or place fertiliser near the plant rather than broadcasting it. Broadcast urea on a hot dry surface loses a large share to the air before the plant sees it. Alternate legumes and cereals. It breaks pest and disease cycles and cuts nitrogen cost. Mulch keeps soil moist, holds temperature down and suppresses weeds. On vegetable plots it can be worth more than an extra irrigation.

I think I have black sigatoka on my plantain and banana. How do I confirm it?

Black sigatoka on plantain and banana can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Dark streaks that widen into blotches with pale centres, starting on older leaves and moving up.

Remove and destroy affected leaves, widen spacing for airflow, and keep the stool desuckered. Nutrition matters, since a well fed plant holds more functional leaves. If what you see in the field does not match this, take a sample to an extension officer rather than guessing.
What is the best approach to stem borers?

Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone. Deadheart in young plants, small holes in stems with frass, and tunnels when a stem is split open.
Sorry, what does that mean exactly?

Destroy or plough in crop residues after harvest to break the carryover, since larvae overwinter in stalks. Early uniform planting across a community reduces pressure for everyone. Deadheart in young plants, small holes in stems with frass, and tunnels when a stem is split open. Put simply: fix the cause, not the symptom, and do the cheap thing first.
Why does it matter how I start keeping rabbits?

Low capital, fast turnover, and they eat forage rather than competing with the household for grain. Housing must stay dry and well ventilated. Overcrowding drives litter moisture, disease and poor growth. It is the most common avoidable mistake in small broiler units.
How do I tell striga apart from other problems on maize, sorghum, millet, upland rice?

Striga on maize, sorghum, millet, upland rice can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Small purple or pink flowered weed emerging near cereal stems, with the crop stunted and yellowed out of proportion to the visible weed.

A striga problem is a soil fertility problem. It thrives where nitrogen and organic matter are depleted. Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available.
What is the right way to manage catfish as they grow?

Catfish cannibalise unevenly sized stock. Grade and sort by size as they grow. Brooders start warm and step down week by week. Chick behaviour is the best gauge: huddling under the heat means too cold, spread to the edges panting means too hot, evenly spread means correct. Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, but only if Newcastle vaccination is kept up. Unvaccinated flocks are periodically wiped out. Ask the older farmers in your area what has worked there, since local experience beats a general rule.

How do I feed cattle through the dry season?

Dry season feed is the binding constraint. Conserve crop residues and plan supplementation before the shortage arrives, not during it. Raised slatted floors keep goats off wet bedding and reduce foot rot and worm burden. Brooders start warm and step down week by week. Chick behaviour is the best gauge: huddling under the heat means too cold, spread to the edges panting means too hot, evenly spread means correct. Conditions differ between zones and soils, so treat this as a starting point.
How do I stop tuta absoluta coming back next season?
1. Exclusion netting over nurseries, pheromone traps for monitoring and mass trapping, removal and destruction of affected material, and rotation away from tomato and related crops.

How do I plant soybean?

1. Rows about 50 to 75cm apart with plants close within the row, aiming for a dense even stand that shades out weeds.
2. Inoculating seed with rhizobium before planting is a small cost that raises nitrogen fixation and yield, especially on land that has not grown soybean before.
How is tomato grown?

Tomato is a staple of West and Central African smallholder systems, known locally as tomati, tatase and shombo are related pepper types. Do the cheapest thing on this list first and give it two weeks before spending more.
What is the right way to use poultry manure safely?

Strong and fast acting. Compost or age it before use, since fresh manure burns young plants and carries weed seed. Persistently poor growth with good rainfall and fertiliser can indicate acidity. Lime works slowly, so apply well ahead of planting. Trees deliberately kept in fields provide shade, fodder, fuel and in the case of nitrogen fixing species a genuine fertility contribution. Choose species that do not compete heavily with the crop.
I have been having stomach pain for three days. What should I take?

That is outside what I can help with. I advise on farming, not on human health, and I am not able to tell you what to take.

Please see a health worker or clinic about pain that has lasted three days.

If you came here with a farm question as well, I am glad to help with that.
I am not sure when to put my cocoa in the ground. Any guidance?

Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Harvest ripe pods regularly rather than in occasional large sweeps. Frequent harvest removes disease sources and reduces losses.
Something is wrong with my oil palm and I cannot tell what. What should I check?

On oil palm a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for harvesting at the wrong ripeness.
- Check for rodent damage to young palms.
- Check for poor drainage.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one.
I have half a hectare and almost no money this season. What is the single best thing I can do for my maize?

Weed on time. If you can only do one thing, that is the one.

Weeding costs labour rather than cash, and on a small maize plot it changes yield more than any input you could buy with the money you do not have. Maize is most vulnerable to competition in its first few weeks, so weeding early matters far more than weeding often.

After that, in order of how much they give back per naira spent:

1. Correct spacing and one plant per stand, which costs nothing but attention at planting.
2. Planting on established rains rather than the first shower, which avoids a replant.
3. If any cash exists, a small amount of nitrogen placed beside the plant at about three to four weeks, rather than broadcast. Placement makes a small quantity work like a larger one.

Avoid spending scarce money on spraying unless you have actually scouted and found a problem worth treating.
How do I deal with fall armyworm on my maize?

Handpicking on small plots, intercropping to break up the stand, encouraging natural enemies, and destroying crop residues after harvest. Damage matters most in early vegetative growth. Late infestation on a tasselled crop rarely justifies treatment cost. Ragged holes and moist sawdust like frass in the whorl. Larvae have an inverted pale Y on the head and four dots in a square on the second to last segment.
Which of those matters most if I can only do one?

Handpicking on small plots, intercropping to break up the stand, encouraging natural enemies, and destroying crop residues after harvest. Damage matters most in early vegetative growth. Late infestation on a tasselled crop rarely justifies treatment cost. Labour costs time rather than money, and on a small plot it changes the outcome more than most purchased inputs.
Something in my house has a fever and is vomiting. What do I do?

Before I answer, I need to know who is sick, because the answer is completely different.

If it is **a person**, especially a child, I cannot advise you at all. Take them to a clinic or health worker today. Fever with vomiting can worsen fast in people.

If it is **an animal**, tell me which one and I can help: a goat, a chicken and a calf all point at different causes, and a vet or extension officer is still the right call if it is severe or spreading through the flock.
My cocoa is not yielding like my neighbour's. What should I change?

1. Prune to keep the canopy open and remove chupons and dead wood. An open canopy dries faster and suffers less black pod.
2. Young cocoa needs shade to establish. Mature trees tolerate more light, but full sun without adequate nutrition shortens the life of the farm.

How do I keep egg shell quality good?

Laying birds need adequate calcium or shells thin and break. Shell quality falling across a flock usually points to calcium or age. Laying birds need a consistent lighting pattern. Erratic light disrupts laying more than most farmers expect. Overcrowding drives litter moisture, disease and poor growth. It is the most common avoidable mistake in small broiler units.
What goes wrong when farmers do not avoid aflatoxin in groundnut and maize?

A mould toxin, worst in groundnut and maize, produced when drying is slow or storage is damp. It is invisible at safe looking levels, causes real harm, and gets consignments rejected. Rapid drying and sorting out damaged and discoloured grain are the practical defences. Write down what you spent, planted, applied and sold. Without records you cannot tell which of your decisions actually made money. Dry on tarpaulin or a raised platform, never on bare ground, which reintroduces moisture, soil and mould.
My maize is not yielding like my neighbour's. What should I change?

1. Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage.
2. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare.
3. Split nitrogen: a basal compound fertiliser at planting, then top dress with urea at about 3 to 4 weeks, and again at knee height on poor soils. Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant, not broadcast, to cut losses.
4. Hybrid seed yields more but must be bought fresh each season. Open pollinated varieties can be saved for 2 to 3 seasons with careful selection, which suits farmers with tight cash.
5. Follows a legume such as cowpea or soybean well, which reduces nitrogen cost.
What actually works against striga?

A striga problem is a soil fertility problem. It thrives where nitrogen and organic matter are depleted.

1. Rotation with legumes, restoring soil fertility and organic matter, hand pulling before the weed flowers and seeds, and resistant varieties where available.
2. Each plant sheds very many long lived seeds, so a single season of letting it flower undoes years of work.

On onion a short list of causes covers most of what goes wrong.

What to look for:
- Check for purple blotch.
- Check for thrips.
- Check for heavy storage losses from poor curing.

Match the symptom to the cause before spending money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one. Ask the older farmers in your area what has worked there, since local experience beats a general rule.

Overcrowding drives litter moisture, disease and poor growth. It is the most common avoidable mistake in small broiler units. Deworm on a schedule appropriate to the season and local advice, since worm pressure rises in the wet season.

I think I have maize streak on my maize. How do I confirm it?

Maize streak on maize can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Fine broken pale streaks running parallel along the leaf, plants stunted when infected young.

Carried by leafhoppers, often from nearby grasses and volunteer maize. Tolerant varieties and avoiding very late or staggered planting near infected stands. There is no cure for an infected plant.
How do I tell bacterial wilt apart from other problems on tomato, pepper, and other solanaceous crops?

Bacterial wilt on tomato, pepper, and other solanaceous crops can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Sudden wilting while leaves stay green. Cut a stem and suspend it in clear water: a milky ooze streaming out confirms it.

No chemical cure. Rotate away from solanaceous crops for several seasons, improve drainage, and remove affected plants with the surrounding soil. Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.

How do I stop groundnut rosette coming back next season?

1. Plant early and at a dense even spacing so the canopy closes quickly, and use resistant varieties where available.

Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
Walk me through planting sweet potato on a small plot.

1. Use vine cuttings about 30cm long taken from healthy vigorous vines, planted into ridges or mounds.
2. Ridges or mounds give the roots room to size up and keep them out of waterlogged soil.

If what you see in the field does not match this, take a sample to an extension officer rather than guessing.

I want to start growing oil palm. Where do I begin?

1. About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls.
2. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.
My maize has holes in the young leaves and there is something like wet sawdust in the centre of the plant. What is this?

That is almost certainly fall armyworm. The wet sawdust you are seeing is frass, the caterpillar's droppings, and finding it packed in the whorl is the giveaway.

Confirm it before you spend anything:

1. Open the whorl of several plants across the field, early morning or late evening when larvae are active.
2. Look for a pale upside down Y marking on the head of the caterpillar.
3. Look for four dark dots arranged in a square near the tail end.

If you find those, it is fall armyworm. Check how many plants out of twenty are affected, because that number decides whether treatment is worth the cost. A few plants with old damage and no live larvae does not justify spraying.
Most of the plants have it. They are about knee high. What do I do?

Knee high is the stage where this pest actually costs you yield, so it is worth acting now. Later infestations on a tasselled crop rarely repay the cost of treatment.

Start with what costs labour rather than cash:

1. Handpick larvae from the whorls if the plot is small enough. Done thoroughly over a few days this works.
2. Destroy badly damaged plants that will not recover rather than nursing them.
3. After harvest, destroy the crop residues, because that is what carries the pest into next season.

If you do decide to spray, use a product registered for fall armyworm on maize and follow the label rate exactly. Direct the spray down into the whorl, since that is where the larvae sit. A spray over the top of the leaves mostly misses them and wastes your money.
Will it come back next season?

It can, and whether it does depends mostly on what you do after this harvest rather than on what you spray now.

The pest survives between seasons in crop residues and on volunteer plants. So clear and destroy the stalks rather than leaving them standing, and remove volunteer maize before the next crop goes in. Planting at the same time as your neighbours also helps, because a staggered planting across a community gives the pest a continuous supply of young maize to move into.

Scout early next season rather than waiting for visible damage. Catching it in the first weeks costs far less than rescuing a knee high crop.
Why does it matter how I dry my harvest properly?

Dry on tarpaulin or a raised platform, never on bare ground, which reintroduces moisture, soil and mould. A simple raised solar dryer dries faster and cleaner than open ground and keeps rain, dust and animals off the crop. Faster drying is directly less mould.
How do I tell groundnut rosette apart from other problems on groundnut?

Groundnut rosette on groundnut can be identified in the field before you treat.

What to look for:
- Stunted bushy plants with small distorted yellowed leaves, often in patches within the field.

Carried by aphids, worst in late planted and sparse stands. Plant early and at a dense even spacing so the canopy closes quickly, and use resistant varieties where available. Check this against what your neighbours are seeing before you act on a whole field.
What is the right way to store grain without chemicals?

Hermetic bags control storage insects without chemicals, but only if the liner is sealed properly every time. Dry grain to roughly 13 percent before storage. Grain that feels dry in the afternoon sun can still be too wet to store safely. Dry on tarpaulin or a raised platform, never on bare ground, which reintroduces moisture, soil and mould.

What actually works against newcastle disease?

1. Vaccination on schedule is the control. There is no treatment once the flock breaks. Local backyard flocks benefit most, since they are usually unvaccinated.
2. Isolate new or returning birds before mixing, restrict visitor access, and never bring birds back from market into the flock unquarantined.
What should I focus on to improve my oil palm?

About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls. Harvest on ripeness judged by loose fruit on the ground, not by a fixed calendar. Underripe bunches give less oil, overripe raises free fatty acid and lowers quality. Plant tenera hybrid seedlings from a reputable source. Dura palms grown from random seed give much thicker shells and less oil.
That sounds expensive. What if I cannot afford it?

About 9m triangular spacing, roughly 143 palms per hectare. Crowded palms shade each other and yield falls. Harvest on ripeness judged by loose fruit on the ground, not by a fixed calendar. Underripe bunches give less oil, overripe raises free fatty acid and lowers quality. The unpaid work usually beats the bought input: clean planting material, correct spacing, and weeding on time.
